chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Hasan from Fadala from Aban from Ismail Al-Ju'fi who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The best making up of supererogatory prayers is night prayer at night and day prayer during the day.' I asked: 'And it would be two Witr prayers in one night?' He said: 'No.' I asked: 'And why do you order me to perform two Witr prayers in one night?' He said: 'One of them is a making up (qada).'

key_terms.قَضَاء: Making up a missed or delayed prayer
key_terms.وَتْر: Witr prayer (odd-numbered prayer, often concluding night prayers)

ai.seo_question: What is the best method for making up missed supererogatory prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of temporal fidelity in making up supererogatory prayers, ensuring that night nafl is compensated at night and day nafl during the day. He clarifies that performing two Witr prayers in one night is not a duplication of the same act, but rather one serves as the makeup (qada) for a previously missed Witr, thereby preserving the integrity of the specific prayer's time. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on maintaining the distinct identity and timing of individual voluntary acts of worship.
